prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show a downward-looking workspace with bowls, pots, sacks, poles, rope and ground spread mostly within about 0.3–2 m of the camera wearer; the brightest forearms, hands and sacks are generally nearest, while the dark ground and upper-edge objects are farther away. Another person is partly visible in frames 2–5, mainly as arms, legs or a yellow-checkered torso near the lower edge, roughly 0.3–1 m away; the head is out of view, so facing direction and gaze cannot be determined. Nearby bowls are separated from one another by roughly 0.2–0.7 m, and several hands, sacks and containers appear within arm’s reach of the wearer or the other person. Across the strip, objects shift laterally as the camera turns over the same area, while hands intermittently approach the sacks and containers; the map makes near–far layering and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB, but its smooth gray regions, abrupt edge halos and inconsistent tones on sacks and thin poles make metric distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation isolates only a small subset of the crowded scene: green bowl masks, a cyan person/arm-shaped region and bottle, plus two thin yellow regions labeled “carrot,” while most pots, sacks, poles, rope, ground and visible body parts remain black. The detected bowl in frame 2 lies left of and roughly 0.2–0.5 m from the cyan person region, and the frame-4 bowl is above-left of a yellow thin object; these items appear approximately 0.4–1.2 m from the camera and mostly within arm’s reach. The masks clarify which image regions the model treats as separate foreground instances even where RGB textures overlap, and their frame-to-frame displacement shows the camera’s lateral turning across the workspace. The map is unreliable for complete spatial layout: detections disappear between adjacent frames, the cyan person and bottle boundaries appear merged or fragmented, the “carrot” labels likely cover thin objects ambiguously, and it provides no dependable depth, facing direction or gaze information.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only two magenta hand skeletons, one in frame 1 near the left side and one in frame 2 near the center-right; both correspond to hands close to the working surface, roughly 0.3–0.7 m from the camera wearer. The hands are surrounded in RGB by bowls, sacks and containers within about 0.1–0.5 m, but no body skeletons are recovered and the people’s heads remain outside the view, so body orientation, facing direction and gaze cannot be established. The first detected hand is farther left and the second appears farther right in the next frame, consistent with camera motion and/or hand movement, after which pose detections disappear despite visible limbs in RGB. The skeletons reveal finger and wrist geometry that is difficult to separate from the cluttered RGB background, but missing limbs, absent detections in frames 3–5 and possible overlap between nearby hands make reach and inter-person distances only approximate.
